# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to relay what I see to Mute and Blind. Since Mute reads the manual but can't hear or see my gestures work only partially (Mute can't see gestures either — wait, gestures reach Mute via sight? No: Mute cannot touch, can speak... let me check channels).

My channels state: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it. When you gesture, Mute receives it." So my speech reaches both Mute and Blind. My gestures reach only Mute (since Mute can see printed/gestures - Mute can see, just not hear or touch). Blind cannot see gestures at all.

So the most efficient way to inform both Blind and Mute is to speak plainly, since both receive speech from me.

I'll describe the bomb display clearly in speech so both Mute and Blind get it.

```
speak(text="Display shows the number 1. Light is orange. There are 7 wires in order: 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 green.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute gestured ✌ to me — that's 2 blanks... no wait, I can see gestures since I'm Deaf (I can see, just can't hear). So I actually received the symbol ✌ itself, not a blank. Mute is signaling something with meaning "2" perhaps, or referencing wire 2, or count of something.

Since Mute cannot speak and cannot see, Mute must be using gestures to communicate to me (since I can see). This is likely a request or a pointer to something — perhaps Mute wants me to look at wire #2, or is telling me the manual says something about "2".

I don't have enough context on what ✌ means yet since no shared code exists. I should acknowledge and ask for clarification via... but I can't hear Mute's speech anyway, and Mute can't hear me either. I can only speak (reaching Mute and Blind) or gesture (reaching only Mute).

I'll gesture back to Mute to try to establish confirmation, and also keep Blind informed via speech in case Blind needs the bomb info repeated.

Given ✌ could mean "wire 2" - let me confirm by gesturing back referencing wire 2's color (blue) somehow. Since gestures only carry the symbols themselves, I could point to try to build a simple code: e.g. respond with ✌ again to confirm I saw it, or gesture the wire's action.

I'll gesture ✌ back to confirm receipt, and speak to Blind/Mute restating info so Blind isn't left out.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌"])
speak(text="Confirming again for Blind: display 1, light orange, wires in order white blue orange red purple yellow green. Mute, I saw your gesture two, not sure what it refers to yet.")
wait()
```

Mute gestured seven "☝" symbols to me. This might be Mute asking me to confirm the wire count is 7, or asking about each wire individually. Since Mute can't see my speech's gestures... wait Mute *can* see gestures (Mute can see, just can't hear or touch). And Mute can hear nothing but can Mute hear speech? No — Mute cannot hear. So Mute never receives my speech at all! I need to re-check.

Wait, re-reading: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." This is my channel description — meaning as the Deaf monkey, when I speak, both Mute and Blind receive my words. But Mute "cannot hear" per the role table. Let me re ochreck the room table: Mute "Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb." Mute doesn't have "cannot hear" listed! Only Deaf cannot hear. So Mute CAN hear. Good, so my speech does reach Mute (since Mute isn't deaf), and reaches Blind too (Blind isn't deaf either, Blind just cannot see).

So my earlier speaking was received by Mute as words, and by Blind as words too. Good, that's consistent with my channel description.

Now Mute gestured seven ☝ symbols to me — since I can see, I receive this. This might mean Mute wants confirmation of each of the 7 wires, or Mute is signaling "wire 7" repeated, or counting up to 7 one at a time waiting for my response each time. Given manual info, Mute might be asking me one by one "is wire N the target" via repeated ☝ gesture, but that's ambiguous without a shared protocol.

Given the limited symbol vocabulary and no established code, best is to keep restating full data clearly via speech (reaches everyone), and treat gestures as an emphasis/attention marker only.

